data_output.description: The fixed training command must write predictions_valid.npz containing exactly two arrays: row_ids and scores. row_ids must be int64 identifiers equal to 0..N-1 in the original encoded validation-row order, and scores must be a finite one-dimensional array of length N aligned positionally with row_ids. Ground truth is loaded only by the fixed evaluator; the model and trainer must not emit labels or reorder validation rows.

model_input.description: model.py must preserve Model(dimension, learning_rate, l2), logits(features), step(features, labels), predict(features, batch_size=...), state(), and load_state(state). features is an N-by-2 int32 array containing offset-encoded user and video IDs, including one unknown bucket per field. The model must produce one finite logit/score per row and train with pointwise binary cross-entropy gradients. Implement separate 16-dimensional embeddings for the full encoded user and video feature spaces, additive user and video weights plus a scalar bias, and score each row as bias + user_weight + video_weight + dot(user_embedding, video_embedding). State checkpointing must include all trainable parameters and restore them exactly; prediction must preserve input row order and contain no labels.
